segments.t: Font, color and cursor overrides for the Snippet Manager and the Snippet Edit dialog. Open via KTPH001Configuration → Global Settings → Snippet EditorKTPH002; stored in KTPH000.
Empty (inherit) or an installed monospace family
One key, optionally with up to three modifiers (Ctrl/Cmd, Shift, Alt)

Click the KTPH018AI Completion ShortcutKTPH019 field and press the combination you want — the field records what you pressed, and KTPH020ResetKTPH021 restores KTPH022KTPH000KTPH023+KTPH024KTPH001KTPH025. A combination is one main key (a letter, digit, function key, KTPH026KTPH002KTPH027, KTPH028KTPH003KTPH029, an arrow, KTPH030KTPH004KTPH031 and so on) with none, one, two or three modifiers, so KTPH032KTPH005KTPH033 alone, KTPH034KTPH006KTPH035+KTPH036KTPH007KTPH037 and KTPH038KTPH008KTPH039+KTPH040KTPH009KTPH041+KTPH042KTPH010KTPH043 are all valid. On macOS the KTPH044KTPH011KTPH045 modifier is the Cmd key, matching the editor's own shortcuts. The new combination applies to snippet editors opened afterwards; KTPH046KTPH012KTPH047+KTPH048KTPH013KTPH049 opens the list as well and cannot be reassigned. Choosing something other than KTPH050KTPH014KTPH051+KTPH052KTPH015KTPH053 gives KTPH054KTPH016KTPH055+KTPH056KTPH017KTPH057 back its normal editor meaning: it removes one level of indentation.

These settings override the terminal/editor defaults for snippet windows only. Leave a field empty — or set the font size to KTPH000 — to inherit the general setting from KTPH001AppearanceKTPH002, KTPH003ColorsKTPH004 and KTPH005EditorKTPH006 instead.
The snippet editor itself, including its AI code actions and language fields, is described under KTPH000SnippetsKTPH001.
